question: According to the Henry Cavendish experiment conducted in 1797-1798, what was the value of the universal constant of gravity?
solution:
The correct answer is **__6.75 × 10-11 N m2/kg2__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__The **Cavendish experiment **was performed in **1797–1798 **by **English scientist Henry Cavendish**.
 
• It was the **first experiment **to **measure **the **force of gravity **between **masses **in the **laboratory **and the **first to yield accurate values **for the **gravitational constant**.
 
• The **Cavendish experiment **was **significant **not only for **measuring Earth's density **(and thus its mass) but also for **proving that Newton's law of gravitation **worked on **scales much **smaller than those of **the solar system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry Cavendish FRS **was an **English natural philosopher **and **scientist **who was an **important experimental and theoretical chemist **and **physicist**. He is noted for **his discovery of hydrogen**, which he termed **"inflammable air".**
 
• He was **born **on **10 October 1731**, **in Nice in France**.
 
• He died on **24 February 1810**, in **London**, **United Kingdom**
